This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The issue is that the HelpFormatter's setArgName() method sets a field defaultArgName in HelpFormatter, but this defaultArgName is never used when printing the usage. In the printUsage() method of HelpFormatter, it iterates over the options in the Options instance and calls appendOption() for each option to build the usage string.

In appendOption(), the logic to add the argument name to the usage is based solely on the Option instance's own argName field, accessed via option.getArgName(), and only if option.hasArgName() returns true (which checks if argName is non-null and non-empty). The HelpFormatter's own defaultArgName is not used anywhere in printUsage() or appendOption().

Looking at the test case, the Option is created via OptionBuilder.hasArg().isRequired().create("f"). From OptionBuilder.create(), we see that it calls option.setArgName(argName) with the current value of OptionBuilder.argName. The default value of OptionBuilder.argName seems to be "arg" (as per the bug report's description: "Option and the OptionBuilder bring automatically a default value 'arg'"). This means the Option already has a non-null argName ("arg") set before being passed to HelpFormatter.

Thus, the test sets HelpFormatter.setArgName("argument"), but since Option has already a set argName ("arg"), appendOption() uses the option's argName ("arg") rather than any HelpFormatter default. This causes the default argument name set on HelpFormatter to have no effect, as the Option's argName overrides it.

The missing link is that HelpFormatter.printUsage() or appendOption() does not check HelpFormatter.defaultArgName at all to override or influence the Option's argument name if the Option already has one set. The design expects the Option's argName to be authoritative, but this behavior is unintuitive and contradicts the test expectation.

Hence, the bug is that HelpFormatter's defaultArgName (set via setArgName) is never used or applied in the usage string generation when the Option already has an argName set, causing the HelpFormatter-wide default argument name to have no effect.

Summary:
- OptionBuilder sets a default argName "arg" on Options.
- HelpFormatter.setArgName() sets a defaultArgName on HelpFormatter but is never used in printUsage().
- appendOption() uses Option.getArgName() if present, not HelpFormatter.defaultArgName.
- Test fails because HelpFormatter's argName override is ignored.
- The root cause is HelpFormatter ignoring defaultArgName and relying solely on the Option's argName.

Next, I can identify the locations in the code that should be fixed based on this diagnosis.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
